dedupe_keys.name: spallation neutron source high voltage converter normal and faulty waveforms

description: Oak Ridge National Laboratory publishes power-converter waveform data from the Spallation Neutron Source linear accelerator. Measurements from more than fifteen high-voltage converter modulators during 2020–2022 are grouped into four subsystems with separate normal/fault labels. Repository documentation gives a 400-nanosecond sampling interval and fourteen signal channels, including currents, voltages and magnetic flux. Preprocessing removes erroneous noise-like traces and retains 1.8-millisecond active pulses. Version 5 provides NumPy arrays, an Excel sample and a Python loading example, free under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is one specialist facility; curated pulses cannot establish calendar failure frequencies or general utility-grid fault rates. A reviewer-assessed use is testing converter fault detection and condition-monitoring assumptions in electrical-system simulations. model-openipsl supplies related electrical dynamic models, but accelerator signals and model states require an explicit mapping. The array files and loader were not downloaded or executed.
